rv.q: This show is way more enjoyable than history class ever was.
"The Great Kahn," though stumbling pacing-wise near the end, casually delivers a gut punch to remind ourselves that we are who we make ourselves.
The script makes you think, and Redtwist Theatre has done a superb job giving it voice and body.
The beginning of the play is brilliant: deadly serious yet wildly comedic.
The confusing and unfinished script is an unwavering obstacle that is impossible to overcome without additional development opportunities.

cn.t: Critics find this coming-of-age story about identity and history has a brilliant, comedic start and lively performances, though one reviewer faults the play for muddling its ambitious examination of the past and present.
